result.topic_en: Hilbert argues that for any mathematical question one can first ask whether it is decidable by finitely many operations, illustrates this with the existence of sextic curves with 11 separate ovals, and notes that not every integrity domain is finitely generated.

items.english: If a mathematical problem, I mean a question A, is posed, then one can first settle the question whether this question A can be settled by a finite number of operations or not.
